questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed my exchange stay in Austin, which is a very lively and active city with plenty of things to do. I was positively surprised by the food culture, especially the strong Mexican influence and the excellent barbecue scene. Campus life at University of Texas at Austin was also a highlight for me, with many opportunities to attend basketball, football, and volleyball games. In addition, there were great options for staying active, and I especially enjoyed swimming in the outdoor pool.

One downside of Austin is its location within Texas, as distances are very large, which makes it harder to travel to other parts of the United States. The city is also very car-oriented, meaning that simple tasks like grocery shopping can be inconvenient without a car. However, renting a bike worked well for everyday transportation, and the Orange Bike Project was a great and affordable option, costing only $50 for an entire semester.

Additional comments:
questions.answer:
A bit difficult we were lucky but you apply after the american students, so a lot off classes was already full. And you have to wait further if you want a class in another faculty.
